title: Entropy from probability
spoken: S minus S nought equals R over N times the natural log of W.
explanation: Einstein's form of Boltzmann's principle in section 5: probabilities of independent states multiply, their entropies add, so entropy is R over N times ln W.
assumptions: Entropy is a smooth function of probability, which Einstein takes for granted.
A foundation lesson's statement in modern notation; not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: The change in entropy
notes.explanation: S minus its value in the reference state.

notes.title: The natural logarithm
notes.explanation: Einstein prints lg; it means ln.

notes.title: R over N
notes.explanation: The gas constant per molecule, now called Boltzmann's constant.

notes.title: Times
notes.explanation: The constant R over N times the logarithm.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Entropy is a logarithm of probability, measured from a reference state.

notes.title: Number of molecules in a mole
notes.explanation: N, the number that turns R into a per-molecule constant.

notes.title: Entropy
notes.explanation: The entropy of the state considered.

notes.title: Gas constant
notes.explanation: R, energy per mole per kelvin.

notes.title: Probability of the state
notes.explanation: W, relative to the reference state.

notes.title: Reference entropy
notes.explanation: S₀, the entropy of the state compared with.

sentence.text: minus its reference value is R over N times the log of the probability
